_comment: Seed transcript for persona-lab. Copy to seed.json (gitignored) and replace with your own context. 'summary' becomes the thread summary the persona sees; 'messages' is the prior conversation history the model reads before answering the prompt under test. Keep it short — long seeds inflate input tokens and can hit provider fault bands. This example is fictional and exists only to show the shape.
summary: A short pairing session reviewing a small caching change. Colleague register: the user and the assistant both know the codebase well.

messages.content: Did the cache change land? Dashboard still shows misses.

It landed, but only half of it took. The read path checks the cache now; the write path still bypasses it on the error branch, so any request that retries repopulates nothing. That's why you see misses clustered right after failures rather than evenly.
Makes sense. Want to fold the write-path fix into the same change or split it?
Same change — splitting it leaves a half-wired cache in main between merges, which is worse than either state alone. One commit, both paths, one review.
